name: River length
question: Length from source to mouth in kilometers. Each gridline step is ten times longer.

items.name: Jordan
items.fact: The Jordan flows into the Dead Sea, the lowest place on land.

items.name: Thames
items.fact: The Thames is tidal for 100 km up to Teddington Lock.

items.name: Shannon
items.fact: The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland and Britain.

items.name: Tiber
items.fact: Legend says Romulus and Remus were set adrift on the Tiber.

items.name: Hudson
items.fact: The Hudson's lower half is a tidal estuary.

items.name: Seine
items.fact: The Seine flows through Paris.

items.name: Loire
items.fact: The Loire is France's longest river.

items.name: Elbe
items.fact: The Elbe flows from the Czech Republic through Germany to the North Sea.

items.name: Rhine
items.fact: The Rhine flows through or along six countries.

items.name: Colorado
items.fact: The Colorado carved the Grand Canyon.

items.name: Ganges
items.fact: The Ganges is sacred in Hinduism.

items.name: Zambezi
items.fact: The Zambezi plunges over Victoria Falls.

items.name: Danube
items.fact: The Danube passes through more countries than any other river: ten.

items.name: Volga
items.fact: The Volga is Europe's longest river.

items.name: Mississippi
items.fact: A raindrop takes about 90 days to travel the whole Mississippi.

items.name: Congo
items.fact: The Congo is the deepest river in the world.

items.name: Mekong
items.fact: The Mekong flows through six countries.

items.name: Yangtze
items.fact: The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia.

items.name: Amazon
items.fact: The Amazon carries more water than the next seven largest rivers combined.

items.name: Nile
items.fact: The Nile and the Amazon still compete for 'longest river', depending on how you measure.
